I was in a coastal mountain range, right next to a river. The set up.

  • Cheapo double hammock from a local outfitter

  • ENO Ember 2 underquilt

  • Cheapo light weight sleeping bag

  • Old school thermarest sleeping pad

  • Two carabiners and paracord

Night one was in the lower 50s. Piece of cake with the sleeping bag on top and the Ember 2 UQ. Nice and warm no issues.

Night two got down into the 40s, I could see my breath. Same setup as night one, got a little chilly. Added the thermarest pad under me and it was almost too warm.

I don't know how much colder I could go with this setup. I think the underquilt would be the weak point. But I was definitely comfy this weekend.
Hammock camped in lower temps than I have before this weekend.

I've been camping in a hammock the past couple times I've gone out. Recently I was up in the high country of Colorado scaling a couple 14r's. I was borrowing my roommate's 0 degree bag and hammock. Ya. With my 0° bag I could go down a lot lower. The thermarest makes a huge difference in temp. Gotta get that insulation under you.
Even in my standard bag, definitely not rated for under 30 degrees, I had a pad underneath me and a wool blanket over top with a tarp above to keep the heat in. Superior to a tent IMO
Easier to pack too. I think my old thermarest is the heaviest part of the setup.
Hammock is the best for lightweight gear.
